title: Let Everyone Get Involved in Opportunities for National Service Act
official_summary:
Let Everyone Get Involved in Opportunities for National Service Act or the LEGION Act

(Sec. 3) This bill expands eligibility for membership in The American Legion to include veterans and servicemembers who served any time after December 7, 1941, including those currently serving. Presently, only veterans and servicemembers who served during periods of war specified by Congress are eligible to join The American Legion.

(Sec. 4) The bill also prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin for the purposes of holding a staff position at The American Legion.

summary.headline: A 2019 law widens who can join The American Legion and bars discrimination in its staff hiring.
summary.what_it_does: The law expands American Legion membership to veterans and current servicemembers who served at any time after December 7, 1941, not just those who served in congressionally specified wartime periods. It also prohibits The American Legion from discriminating based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin when filling staff positions.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who served after December 7, 1941, outside designated war periods
who_it_affects.how: They become eligible to join The American Legion, which previously limited membership to those who served in specified wartime periods.
They become eligible to join The American Legion, including while still on active service.

who_it_affects.group: The American Legion and its staff applicants
who_it_affects.how: The organization must not discriminate by race, color, religion, sex, or national origin when hiring for staff positions.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 30, 2019; the official summary does not describe a separate effective date.
